newsitem.title: UK: BRITAIN'S PRINCESS DIANA SAID CAUGHT IN SPY VIDEO.
newsitem.headline: BRITAIN'S PRINCESS DIANA SAID CAUGHT IN SPY VIDEO.

text.p: A "spy video" apparently showing Princess Diana in sports pants and bra with her lover James Hewitt was shown on British television on Tuesday in the latest scandal to rock the royal family.

The tabloid Sun, which broke news of the grainy 80-second film, said on Tuesday it confirmed Diana's fears that she had been under secret surveillance during the break-up of her 15-year marriage to heir to the throne Prince Charles.
Buckingham Palace denied the black-and-white video was used as a bargaining chip in her divorce with Charles, finalised in August.
Sky Television broadcast the video, which appeared to show Diana stripping down to cycling pants and sports bra, kissing Hewitt, riding on his back and playfully pillow-fighting.
Diana has previously claimed that her telephone calls were bugged. Transcripts of alleged calls she made to male friends have been printed in British newspapers.
Diana has admitted adultery with Hewitt and, in a sensational television interview in November, said she had "adored" him during their five-year affair.

Hewitt, a cavalry officer who served in the Gulf War, was condemned as a cad and a bounder by fellow officers in 1994 when journalist Anna Pasternak published "Princess in Love", a romantic "faction" account of Hewitt's affair with the princess.
Hewitt told the tabloid: "I am convinced there were illicit spying operations -- undoubtedly, undoubtedly."
"I heard about some tapes and some films of us together and one theory was that the princess's divorce settlement was only half what she wanted because of this sort of material," he said.
